title: Chapter 96 — Prompting Craft
intro: How to get useful results from AI tools — the art of asking the right question the right way.

sections.title: Be Specific
sections.content:
Vague prompts produce vague results. 'Tell me about dishwashers' gives you a textbook overview. 'Compare the Bosch 500 and 800 series dishwashers for a customer with an open-concept kitchen who prioritizes quiet operation and drying performance' gives you a usable selling comparison.

Include context: the customer's situation, their priorities, the specific products, and what you need the output for. The more context you provide, the more useful the response.

Include format: 'Give me three bullet points for the FAB presentation' or 'Draft a follow-up email for a customer who needs to discuss with their spouse' tells the AI exactly what shape the output should take.

sections.title: Iterate, Don't Start Over
sections.content:
If the first response is close but not right, refine it. 'That comparison is good but emphasize the noise level difference more — the customer mentioned it three times during discovery.' This iterative approach produces better results faster than starting from scratch.

Save your best prompts. When you find a prompt that consistently produces great product comparisons, follow-up emails, or objection responses, save it as a template. Build a personal prompt library for your most common tasks.

sections.title: Appliance-Specific Prompting
sections.content:
For product comparisons: 'I am comparing [Product A] and [Product B] for a customer who [situation]. Their top priority is [priority]. Give me a FAB-structured comparison highlighting the key differentiator for this customer.'

For follow-up emails: 'Draft a day-3 follow-up email for [customer name] who visited looking at [product]. They were concerned about [objection]. Include one value-add fact they did not know.'

For roleplay: 'You are a customer who wants a $600 dishwasher and I am the salesperson trying to step them up to the $900 model. Push back on price. I will practice my response.'

For account prep: 'I am meeting with a custom builder who does 15 luxury homes per year. They currently use a competitor for appliances. What questions should I ask in the first meeting and what should my capability pitch include?'
